clue.text: Turn out to be openly gay, but son's accepted

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to come out is to be openly gay, so 'out' fits here
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A remark about someone coming out, with a son who is accepted by the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' means expel. 'Out' (openly gay) takes in S for son: 'son's' reads as 'son is', and 'accepted' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone out is to expel or eject them, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Periodical table may be of such a type

definitions.meaning: happening from time to time, now and then

definitions.text: table may be of such a type
definitions.meaning: a small table for ... use, a common furniture term

explanation.surface: A magazine's table of contents could be of this type.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodical means recurring now and then; a small movable table is also called by this name.

clue.text: Flap putting brake on pre-emptive story

definitions.meaning: a hinged panel on an aircraft wing raised to slow it down
a story published to steal the thunder of a rival's scoop

explanation.surface: A newspaper panics and runs a story first to beat a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan shows the first letter of 'brake' smudged. 'Flap' sounds like a panic, but it is the panel on an aircraft wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a wing panel that disrupts airflow to slow a plane, and a story that ruins a rival's exclusive.

clue.text: One gets to try a mum with it, unfortunately

definitions.text: One gets to try a mum with it, unfortunately

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: something that turns out unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A child is bound to test a mother's patience, alas.
explanation.walkthrough: I (one) joins the letters of TRY A MUM and IT, and 'unfortunately' tells you to rearrange the lot. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: childishness is what tries a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish behaviour is exactly what tests a mother's patience, so the whole clue describes the quality.

clue.text: Aconite that's put on partially bald heads

definitions.meaning: a poisonous plant, also called wolfsbane

definitions.text: that's put on partially bald heads
definitions.meaning: the cowl worn by a cleric whose head is tonsured, shaved on top

explanation.surface: A poisonous plant that sits on balding heads.
explanation.walkthrough: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk's head; the plant's hooded flower gives it its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite is another name for this plant; the cowl of a tonsured cleric also fits literally.

clue.text: Tree turning crimson lake by start of autumn

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
turning round means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A tree goes deep red beside a lake as autumn begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' gives DER. Crimson is just a shade of red, a common crossword step.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family that grows in damp places.

clue.text: Cones damaged when unboxed outside? Wafers may not end up so

definitions.text: Wafers may not end up so

indicators.note: one piece is outside another, wrapping round it

parts.note: taken out of a crate, so not crated

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ice-cream cones arrive broken after being unpacked, and the wafers may suffer too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' gives CONSE. The wafers are communion wafers, consecrated in the Mass, not ice-cream wafers as the cones suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Communion wafers that are never blessed by a priest remain not made holy.

clue.text: Confused singers coming in

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muddled choir walks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act of entering, a formal synonym for coming in.

clue.text: Talk at length about North American

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to yak is to chatter on and on

explanation.surface: Chatting endlessly about a person from North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North American' looks like one phrase; N comes from North and only 'American' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is informal slang for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Accepting defeat, prisoner lands in the soup

indicators.note: a word accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a con is a convict, so a prisoner
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A convict who has given up ends up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lands in the soup' sounds like getting into trouble, but it describes a small piece of fried bread that is dropped into soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube of fried bread that is dropped into soup to garnish it, a playful descriptive definition.

clue.text: Recruited by board, was in charge of game that's not fixed

indicators.note: something recruited by a group is taken into it

parts.note: a table is a board, as in a meal table
ran means managed or was in charge of
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: A company director, taken on by the board, ran a game that is unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be moved from place to place is portable, not fixed in position.

clue.text: Plane shape from study involving Concorde's nose in the past

indicators.note: a word involving others wraps round them

parts.note: a den is a private study room

indicators.note: the nose of something is its front, so the first letter

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A geometric figure from a study of Concorde's former nose cone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests the aircraft, given Concorde, but here it is the geometric sense: a flat figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-sided polygon is a flat figure, a shape drawn on a geometric plane.

clue.text: Confidence giving one cover for life?

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: insurance on yourself, cover for one's own life

explanation.surface: Life insurance is said to give you confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Confidence means trust in oneself; whimsically it also means insurance cover taken out on oneself.

clue.text: As British theatre after 1968 once nudes run riot

indicators.note: to run riot is to go wild, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: After 1968 nudity ran wild on the British stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Theatres Act 1968 abolished the Lord Chamberlain's power to censor plays in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage censorship by the Lord Chamberlain ended in 1968, so British theatre was then free from cuts.

clue.text: Socialist craftsman loses millions making perfume ingredient

indicators.note: a word that loses something has a letter taken away

parts.note: William Morris, the Victorian designer and craftsman, was a committed socialist

explanation.surface: A left-wing artisan loses his fortune and makes scent.
explanation.walkthrough: William Morris was a Victorian designer, craftsman and socialist. Take M away from MORRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris root, from an iris, is dried and powdered for use in perfumes.

clue.text: Switch positions crossing oceans in this slack period

indicators.note: one piece crossing another spans it, so it sits round it

parts.note: the two positions of a switch are off and on
seas are oceans

explanation.surface: Moving between jobs across the sea during a quiet time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' means the oceans sit between the two switch positions, which stay in their natural order.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet time of year for a business such as tourism, a synonym for a slack period.

clue.text: Criminal blasting out foul noise

indicators.note: letters blasted out are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain blaring out a horrible din.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonious means relating to felony, so it is a synonym for criminal.

clue.text: Snobbish about individual reflecting with a nasal voice?

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the whole is read in reverse
about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: la-di-da means affectedly posh or snobbish
an individual is one

explanation.surface: A snob thinking about one person sounds as if talking through the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts one inside the snob's word, and 'reflecting' turns LADIONEDA round. The question mark flags that adenoidal describes a voice only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged adenoids make speech sound blocked and nasal, so the adjective describes such a voice.

clue.text: It's attractive to miss out the fine print

indicators.note: to miss something out is to leave it off, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: fetching means attractive
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Attractive, yes, but skip the small print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine print' looks like a phrase; 'fine' gives F, removed from FETCHING, and 'print' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from an acid-etched metal plate.

clue.text: Turn back in regret — such a dishonest person

indicators.note: one piece goes in another

parts.note: rue means regret

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Turning back in remorse, such a cheat repents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives OG, and 'in' sets it inside the regret word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a scoundrel or cheat, a synonym for a dishonest person.

clue.text: It's hard to eat corn before it's ground extremely little

parts.note: grist is grain that is ready to be milled

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Corn is tough to eat until it has been ground fine.
explanation.walkthrough: GRIST is followed by L and E, the first and last letters of 'little'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is tough cartilage in meat, notoriously hard to chew.

clue.text: Big switch for Hornblower, causing ratings to suffer

definitions.text: Big switch for Hornblower, causing ratings to suffer

parts.words: Big switch for Hornblower, causing ratings to suffer
parts.note: a switch is a whip; Hornblower is the fictional naval captain, and ratings are ordinary sailors who were flogged with this many-thonged whip

explanation.surface: A big change for a TV drama that makes its viewing figures drop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a TV series losing viewers. In fact a switch is a whip, Horatio Hornblower is C S Forester's fictional naval officer, and ratings are ordinary sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval whip with nine knotted cords was used to flog ordinary seamen.

clue.text: Currently at home one loses in such a situation

definitions.text: one loses in such a situation

parts.note: now means at present, currently
in means at home

explanation.surface: A player at home now loses whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where every outcome is a loss, the idiom described.

clue.text: Help to conserve river that's very dry

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Aid is needed to save a river that has dried up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means parched, lacking moisture, a synonym for very dry.

clue.text: Wide range of colours of East End artist?

definitions.meaning: the arc of colours seen in the sky after rain
an RA (Royal Academician) living in Bow, a district of London's East End

explanation.surface: A Cockney painter's palette contains every colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as RA IN BOW: an RA (Royal Academician) living in Bow, a district of London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: The full band of the spectrum seen in the sky, and loosely any wide range.

clue.text: One no longer inexperienced sort led astray

indicators.note: led astray means taken off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone once naive has been led into bad ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An old person has long since stopped being inexperienced, so the phrase is a cryptic description.

clue.text: Tenacity to make son send Easter gift back

parts.note: to do something is to make it

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read in reverse together

parts.note: an egg is the traditional Easter gift

explanation.surface: A determined effort to get a child to return an Easter present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives GGEDNES, turning send and the gift together; the son's S has to go at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistence and determination, a synonym for tenacity.

clue.text: Hated missing trial action

indicators.note: missing means without, so letters are taken away

parts.note: detested means hated
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: An unpopular trial goes ahead without a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TEST out of DETESTED, leaving DE + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is something done, an act, so a synonym for action.
